clue.text: No potent replies to malicious message in writing

indicators.note: malice twists things out of shape, so the preceding words are bent into a new order

parts.note: all fifteen letters used as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot answer effectively responds with a spiteful anonymous note instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'malicious' does double work in spirit: it rearranges the letters and colours the definition, since a poison-pen letter is spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison-pen letter is an anonymous, spiteful note sent through the post, a written communication meant to wound.

clue.text: Co-operating as a tug-of-war team

definitions.meaning: first meaning: working jointly towards a shared goal
second meaning: literally hauling a rope in unison

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is the literal picture behind the idiom: a tug-of-war team all heaving on the rope at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means working jointly in harmony, borrowed from the image of people hauling on a rope at once.

clue.text: Getting through to farms about ground that's always frozen

parts.note: per means by way of, as in 'per post'

indicators.note: turned about means moved around, so these letters are set in a fresh order

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is reaching the farms on account of ground that never thaws.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is soil or rock that stays below freezing all year round, typical of Arctic regions.

clue.text: Height of land round ancient city

indicators.note: one thing set round another encloses it, so the first word wraps the second

parts.note: a state is a country or land
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A surveyor notes the elevation of terrain surrounding a ruined old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's natural standing height, so the two words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Dregs of society writing back about copper

indicators.note: placed about something means wrapped around it
sent back means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A writer pens a piece about policemen, called coppers, as the lowest of the low.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a contemptuous term for the most worthless people, the lowest layer of a community.

clue.text: Slyly taking advantage of towing a racing car?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tricking or deceiving someone

definitions.note: a whimsical literal reading of the phrase
definitions.meaning: second meaning: literally hauling along a speedy vehicle

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the silly literal sense: towing is hauling, and a racing car is a quick vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means deceiving someone or getting away with a trick, while the literal reading hauls a speedy vehicle.

clue.text: And not the navy, having one about to disembark here

definitions.note: the place where one would disembark, a noun pointed at by an adverb

parts.note: nor joins two negatives
taken as written
RN is the Royal Navy
Roman numeral one
re means concerning
to land is to come ashore from a ship

explanation.surface: Passengers, but not sailors, are about to come ashore at a particular port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' and 'to disembark' are separate pieces. 'here' points to the place where you land.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue sketches arriving by sea at a place, and Northern Ireland is the province where the boat lands.

clue.text: Little Maureen met nun refurbishing shrine

parts.note: Mo is a pet form of the name Maureen

indicators.note: refurbishing remakes something, so these letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Maureen bumps into a nun who is restoring a holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrine erected to honour someone is a memorial structure, the same thing as a commemorative edifice.

clue.text: Getting mug with nothing in against a voucher

indicators.note: with something in means holding it inside

parts.note: a mug is a drinking cup
zero looks like the letter O
as in a bet laid on a horse, for or against it

explanation.surface: Someone receives an empty mug in exchange for a token.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a ticket or slip exchangeable for goods or a discount, which is what a voucher is.

clue.text: Youth leader in a squalid neighbourhood seeking shelter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the next

parts.note: a slum is a run-down urban district

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: opening letter of youth

explanation.surface: A gang leader from a run-down estate is looking for refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum is protection or refuge, especially that granted by a state to a political refugee.

clue.text: Mould seen outside at a religious building

indicators.note: a building standing outside a word surrounds it

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fungus is spotted on the exterior of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' looks like fungus growing on a church wall, but it is a pattern for shaping things.
explanation.definitionFit: A template is a pattern or shaped guide used to reproduce a form, just as a mould shapes material.

clue.text: Unidentified girl admits nothing …

indicators.note: admitting lets something in, so the name takes in the other piece

parts.note: a common girl's name
zero looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A young woman confesses that she has nothing, trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, used for an author whose name is unknown.

clue.text: … about going into back of athlete''s Herald

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so one piece sits inside the rest
back here means turned backwards, so the little word after it is read right to left

parts.note: taken as written
a runner is a track athlete
re means concerning

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a girl's empty-handed story concerns a sports newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' looks like the rear of the athlete, but 'back' turns the word 'of' round. 'Herald' with a capital looks like a newspaper title; here it is one who goes ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner is a precursor who announces or anticipates what comes later, just as a herald proclaims an arrival.

clue.text: Put elsewhere, wild ponies riot

indicators.note: wild things run out of control, so these letters scatter into new places

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Untamed horses rampage and have to be moved to another field.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposition something is to move it to a different place, which is to put it somewhere else.

clue.text: Name people not coming back around one

parts.note: men are people

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word is read in the opposite direction
around means surrounding the next item

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A host lists the guests who will not be returning for another round.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention someone is to refer to them by name in passing, so the verb name fits.

clue.text: Needing soft water on board for minor injuries?

indicators.note: something on board a ship is inside it, so the pieces go inside the vessel

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the usual crossword ship
p for piano, the musical term for softly
rain is falling water

explanation.surface: Sailors with minor injuries need gentle hydration aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprains are wrenched ligaments, common minor injuries; the question mark allows they are not always slight.

clue.text: Sporting violation not acceptable to team

parts.note: behaviour that is off is unacceptable
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A foul in a game is something the players refuse to tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Offside is an infringement in football and other games where a player is ahead of the ball illegally.

clue.text: Poles decline to meet employees

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken
staffs are bodies of workers

explanation.surface: People from Poland refuse to sit down with the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' with a capital suggests people from Poland; here it means upright staves.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstaffs are tall vertical posts from which banners are flown, so they are a kind of pole.

clue.text: Spacious and on first class lines

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as the letter I
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A first-class rail carriage is roomy.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is a classic crossword spelling of AI: the digit 1 stands for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is open and well ventilated, with plenty of space and light.

clue.text: Posts as it's not folded

indicators.note: folding something changes its shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Letters are sent as they are, without being folded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posts' suggests mail sent flat; it is a noun for assigned places of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is a place where a sentry or worker is assigned to stand, in the sense of a duty post.

clue.text: Only student less than 10 stone!

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner driver, a student
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Only a learner weighing under ten stone could manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: '10 stone' reads as a body weight, but the number and the unit belong to separate parts of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Story about an island race that's mere gossip

indicators.note: about means wrapped round the following item

parts.note: a tale is a story
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the Isle of Man motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A tale concerning a motorbike race on an island is only idle chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattle is idle chatter and gossip, talk about other people's business of little weight.

clue.text: Girl's simple article overlooked heterodoxy

parts.note: her, as in belonging to a girl

indicators.note: something overlooked is left out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: easy means simple
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A girl's straightforward essay missed unorthodox views.
explanation.definitionFit: Heresy is belief contrary to accepted doctrine, the opposite of orthodoxy, which heterodoxy also names.

clue.text: Doctor acknowledging cause of death?

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
owning up is acknowledging

explanation.surface: A physician admits responsibility for a patient's demise.
explanation.definitionFit: Drowning, suffocation in water, is one of many ways to die, hence the question mark for an example.
